outputs.exact_statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex threefold with $K_X\simeq\mathcal O_X$. For any $B_*\in N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}$ and $H_*\in\operatorname{Amp}(X)$ there are open neighborhoods $V$ of $B_*$ and $W$ of $H_*$ and one $T>0$ such that, for all $B\in V$, $H\in W$ and $t\geq T$, the following hold.* 1. *$(Z_{B,tH},\mathcal A_{B,tH})$ is a geometric numerical stability condition with support on $K_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb R}$.* 2. *There is a geometric numerical stability condition, with support on the same full numerical space, whose charge is exactly $$Z^{\mathrm{LV}}_{B,tH}(E) =-\int_Xe^{-B-itH}\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}(E)\sqrt{\mathop{\mathrm{td}}(X)}, \qquad \sqrt{\mathop{\mathrm{td}}(X)}=1+\frac{c_2(X)}{24}.$$ Its heart is the one constructed in Section 2.

For every polarized smooth projective threefold $(X,H)$ there is $R_*>0$ such that, if $$\alpha>f(\beta):=\frac{\beta^2+R_*^2}{2},$$ then $Q_{\alpha,\beta}(v_H(E))\geq0$ for every nonzero semistable object in $\mathcal B_{H,\beta H}$ for the slope $$\frac{v_2-\beta v_1+(\beta^2-\alpha)v_0}{v_1-\beta v_0},
 \qquad
 v_H(E)=(H^3\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_0(E),H^2\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_1(E),H\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_2(E),\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_3(E)),$$ again interpreted as $+\infty$ at zero denominator.

Let $C$ be an elliptic curve, let $n\ge1$, and fix positive rational numbers $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_n$. For rational $R\ge1$, put $w_r=R\rho_r$ and let $H_r$ be the point-divisor class from the $r$th factor of $C^n$. The product stability condition with charge $$Z_{\mathbf w}(u)=-\int_{C^n}e^{-i\sum_rw_rH_r}\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}(u)$$ has support on the coordinate lattice $$x_I(u)=H_I\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_{n-|I|}(u),\qquad
 H_I=\prod_{r\in I}H_r,\qquad I\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}.$$ More precisely, set $y_I=(\prod_{r\in I}w_r)x_I$. In these coordinates, $$Z_{\mathbf w}(u)=\widehat Z_n(y(u)),\qquad
 \widehat Z_n(y)=-\sum_I(-i)^{|I|}y_I.$$ For a fixed Euclidean norm there is $C_n>0$, independent of $R$, such that $$\|y(u)\|\le C_n|Z_{\mathbf w}(u)|
 \qquad(u\text{ the class of a semistable object}).$$ The constants can be chosen uniformly when the positive ratios $\rho_r$ vary in a compact set. Point sheaves are stable of phase $1$.

Let a stability condition have support on a finite-rank lattice $\Lambda$. Suppose that an object $E$ has primitive class in $\Lambda$ and remains semistable throughout a neighborhood which is open in all central charges $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(\Lambda,\mathbb C)$. Then $E$ is stable.

For every $0<\epsilon<1/8$, there are open neighborhoods $V\ni B_*$ and $W\ni H_*$ in the real divisor and ample spaces, and $T\ge1$, such that for all $B\in V$, $H\in W$, and $t\ge T$, the charge [eq:deformed-ambient-charge] lifts to a stability condition with slicing at distance less than $\epsilon$ from $\mathcal R_t$. The construction is available in an open neighborhood of that charge in the full space $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(K_{\mathrm{num}}(Y),\mathbb C)$.

For either factor in [eq:two-character-factors], the choices in Lemma 9 can be made so that every $B\in V,H\in W,t\ge T$ gives a locally finite geometric stability condition on $X$, with charge [eq:exact-restricted-charge] and full numerical support. Every point sheaf is stable of phase $1$. For $\Theta=1$, the construction also gives compatible geometric slicings on every smooth section $S_h\in|L_h|$, with Harder–Narasimhan phases computed by pushforward to $Y$.

Let $S$ be a smooth projective surface and $(Z,\mathcal R)$ a locally finite geometric stability condition, normalized so that point sheaves have phase $1$. Suppose $$\Im Z(G)=\omega\bigl(c_1(G)-\beta\mathop{\mathrm{rk}}(G)\bigr),$$ where $\omega$ is a real ample divisor class and $\beta$ a real divisor class. Then $$\mathcal R(0,1]=\langle\mathcal F_{\omega,\beta}[1],
                              \mathcal T_{\omega,\beta}\rangle,$$ where $\mathcal T_{\omega,\beta}$ has strictly positive slope factors (including torsion) and $\mathcal F_{\omega,\beta}$ has nonpositive slope factors.
An object of $\mathcal B\cap\mathcal P(1)$ is a zero-dimensional sheaf.
For $E\in\mathcal B$ the denominator in [eq:physical-second-slope] is nonnegative. If it vanishes, then $\Im Z_{B,tH}(E)\ge0$, with equality only for a zero-dimensional sheaf.
For the factor $\Theta=1$ throughout the real sector of Proposition 10, $$\mathcal P(0,1]=\mathcal A_{B,tH}.$$

An object $E\in\mathcal B_{H,B}$ has $d_B(E)\ge0$. Write $n=w_B-a^2r/2$. If $d_B(E)=0$, then $n(E)\ge0$, with equality exactly when $E$ is a zero-dimensional sheaf, including the zero object. For a finite-slope object $E$, semistability is equivalent to the condition that every proper nonzero subobject has positive denominator and slope at most $\nu(E)$. Every finite-slope quotient of a finite-slope semistable object has slope at least $\nu(E)$.

For fixed $a>0$ there is a constant $C_a$, depending only on $a,X,H$, such that every tilt-semistable object, at any real twist $B$, satisfies $$\label{eq:tilt-support-bound}
 |r|+|w_B|+\|c_B\|\le C_a(d_B+|n|),\qquad n=w_B-a^2r/2.$$ The constants can be bounded uniformly when $a$ ranges in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$.

Every nonzero finite-slope tilt-semistable object has a finite filtration in $\mathcal B_{H,B}$ whose factors are tilt-stable of the same finite slope. Extensions of finite-slope semistable objects of the same slope are semistable of that slope.

Suppose $E$ is tilt-semistable of finite slope $u$ at $(a,b)$. Put $c=b+u$ and $R=\sqrt{a^2+u^2}$. Then $E$ is tilt-semistable at every point $$\label{eq:tilt-semicircle}
 b'=c+x,\qquad a'=\sqrt{R^2-x^2},\qquad -R<x<R,$$ and its slope there is $-x$. In particular it is semistable of slope zero at $(R,c)$.

There is an integer $m>0$, depending only on $X,H$, such that every smooth $S\in|H|$ satisfies $$\label{eq:surface-fixed-m} h^0(S,\mathcal O_S(mH))=\chi(\mathcal O_S(mH)), \qquad \mu(K_S)-m\le-1,$$ and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(mH))\to H^0(S,\mathcal O_S(mH))$ is surjective. One can choose relatively compact analytic neighborhoods of a smooth transverse pair of divisors in $|H|\times|mH|$ such that the resulting surfaces and curves, equipped with the induced Fubini–Study metrics, have uniform smooth local geometry.* *Within these neighborhoods one may impose, for each application, the very-general restriction conditions of Lemma 22 and exactness of any specified finite collection of restricted sequences. Restrictions of a specified finite collection of torsion-free sheaves may also be required to remain torsion-free. For a specified bounded complex, one may require its derived restriction to have ordinary cohomology equal to the restrictions of its ordinary cohomology sheaves.

Fix a real number $M$. There is a number $A_0$, depending only on $X,H,B_0,M$ and the chosen smooth neighborhoods, with the following property. For $A\ge A_0$ and a finite set $I\subset\{t\in\mathbb Z:t\le M\}$, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every chosen surface $S$, every $b\in[-1,1]$, every finite collection of slope-stable torsion-free sheaves $G_i$ on $S$, and every $t\in I$, $$\label{eq:negative-surface-cohomology}
 \sum_i h^1(S,G_i(tH))
 \le C\sum_i r_i\left(
  \left\|\frac{c_1(G_i)}{r_i}-T\right\|^2+\xi_{G_i}\right),
 \qquad T=B_0|_S+(b-A)H.$$ The constant is independent of the collection and its ranks. The same upper bound holds for $h^1(S,G(tH))$ if the $G_i$ are the factors of a filtration of $G$. In particular, a bound $C_0e$ for the sum on the right gives a bound $CC_0e$ for the first cohomology.

Let $E\in\mathcal B_{H,B_0+bH}$ be finite-slope $\nu_{A,b}$-semistable with $\nu_{A,b}(E)=0$ and $|b|\leq1$. Put $B=B_0+bH$ and $e=d_B(E)-A|r(E)|$. Let $P$ be the residual term in [eq:positive-residual-triangle] when $r(E)\geq0$, or in [eq:negative-residual-triangle] when $r(E)\leq0$. Let $W\subset\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(\mathcal O_X(-tH),P)$ be any finite-dimensional subspace, where $t_0

Let $G$ be a slope-semistable torsion-free sheaf on a smooth projective complex variety $Y$ with a fixed very ample class. There is a model and a localization on which the geometric fibers of $G$ are torsion-free and slope-semistable. Finitely many such requirements may be imposed simultaneously.

On a smooth projective geometric fiber in characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a slope-semistable torsion-free sheaf of rank $r$. For a constant $c_Y$ fixed by the chosen model of $Y$ and its polarization, $$\label{eq:frobenius-slope-gap}
 \mu_{\max}(F^*G)\leq p\mu(G)+c_Y(r-1).$$

Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex threefold, let $H$ be an ample integral divisor, and let $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ be a smooth integral divisor such that $H|_D=-D|_D$. Fix $B_0\in N^1(X)_{\mathbb Q}$, and set $B=B_0+bH$. If $F$ is a torsion-free sheaf of positive rank on $D$ and $i_*F$ is $\nu_{a,b}$-semistable of slope zero, then $$\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_3^B(i_*F)}{H^2\mathop{\mathrm{ch}}_1^B(i_*F)}\le\frac1{24}.
 \label{eq:exceptional-uniform}$$ Consequently these objects satisfy the corrected strong inequality with $\Gamma=H^2/24$ for every $a>0$, and the uncorrected strong inequality for every $a\ge1/2$. Both constants are independent of $F$, its rank, and $b$.
